text: Seed dormancy (ដំណេករោប់) is the natural resting state of freshly harvested rice seed: even when sown right away after harvesting and threshing, it will not germinate, because the embryo is still dormant. Understanding this matters for two reasons - it explains why newly harvested seed may appear to have poor germination even though it is perfectly healthy, and it matters directly to farmers who want to harvest a seed crop and resow it quickly without a full standard sun-drying period. To break dormancy artificially: first reduce seed moisture to around 5% at a temperature of 25-30°C, then hold the seed at 50°C for 5 consecutive days. Where no drying equipment is available for this controlled process, farmers can instead sun-dry the seed directly, but should avoid the hottest midday hours (roughly 12:00 to 2:00 pm), since excessive heat during that window can damage seed viability rather than simply breaking dormancy. Caution: if moisture is not first brought down to around 5% before heat treatment, direct heat can damage the embryo and lower germination instead of releasing dormancy safely - the moisture reduction step should not be skipped.
